periods.time: Immediately before the 62nd Seven Stars Sword-Art Festival opens

name.zh: 晓学园宣言引发国家危机
name.en: Akatsuki Academy Declaration Splits Public Opinion

periods.summary: Prime Minister Bakuya Tsukikage's creation of National Akatsuki Academy and attack on Hagun turn Seven Stars into a political referendum. Public opinion divides between those who reject his coercive methods and those who support Japan reclaiming Blazer education and leaving the League's influence.
periods.cause: Tsukikage publicly breaks the custom of entrusting Blazer education to the International Mage-Knight League and uses Akatsuki's strength as proof of national independence.
periods.process: Citizens debate whether Japan should remain within the League, whether Akatsuki's attack was fabricated or harmless because it used Fantasy Form, and whether Japan should stop serving other nations' wars.
periods.outcome: The upcoming Seven Stars tournament is framed as a contest that could sway Japan toward either remaining in the League or moving toward complete independence.
periods.significance: Sets the political stakes for all tournament matches in this volume.
